q: 1. Pick up the component not applicable to aeroplanes ...........
explain: Wings provide lift, engines provide power, and the air screw (propeller) provides thrust; all are standard components of traditional aeroplanes.

q: 2. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following ...........
options: in single engine aeroplanes, the engine is provided in the nose of the aircraft
in double engine aeroplanes, one engine on either wing is placed symmetrically
in three engine aeroplanes, two engines are placed on both wings and one engine is placed in the tail
explain: In many three-engine configurations (like the DC-10), one engine is in the tail and the other two are under the wings, but the statement 'on both wings' (plural) implies multiple per wing or a specific symmetry not universally 'incorrect' except in the context of standard textbook definitions for sub-engineers.

q: 3. Pick up the correct statement from the following ...........
options: minimum turning radius of aircrafts decides the size of the apron and the radius of the curves at taxi-ends
take off and landing distances for an aircraft, determine the minimum runway length
the length of the normal haul of the air craft decides the frequency of operation
explain: All these factors are fundamental design criteria in airport engineering for determining spatial requirements and infrastructure capacity.

q: 4. Pick up the component not applicable to aeroplanes
explain: Wings, engines, air screws (propellers), and the fuselage are all essential components of an airplane.

q: 5. The distance between main gears is 10 m, and the distance of nose gear from centre of main gears is 30 m. If the angle of turning is 60°, the distance of centre of rotation from the nearer main gear, is ...........
explain: Using trigonometry for the turning radius: $R = b \cdot \cot(\theta)$. Distance from the center of rotation to the nearer gear involves subtracting half the gear tread.

q: 6. *The fuselage includes
explain: The fuselage is the central body of an aircraft that houses the crew, passengers, and cargo.

q: 7. Wing loading of an aircraft is ............
options: gross total weight of the aircraft / load of wings
gross total weight of the aircraft / wing area
gross total weight of the aircraft / total available H.P. of engines
explain: Wing loading is defined as the total weight of the aircraft divided by the total wing area ($W/S$).

q: 8. *Fuselage is parts of aircraft for accommodation of
explain: Modern fuselages are designed to accommodate passengers, cargo, and necessary service facilities.

q: 9. Pick up the correct statement from the following ...........
options: landing speed is directly proportional to the wing loading
wing loading remaining constant, the take off distance is directly proportional to the powder loading
explain: Higher wing loading increases stall speed (and thus landing speed). Power loading (weight/horsepower) directly affects acceleration and takeoff distance.

q: 10. *Ramp is a
explain: A ramp (air stairs) is a mobile wheeled staircase used for embarking and disembarking passengers.

q: 11. *The maximum value of angle of turning of the nose gear for large jet aircrafts, is limited to
explain: For large aircraft, the nose gear turning angle is limited to 60° to avoid excessive tire wear and structural stress.

q: 12. Conical surface of the approach area rises outwards ...........
explain: The conical surface extends from the periphery of the inner horizontal surface at a slope of 1 in 20 (5%).

q: 13. Pick up the correct statement from the following ...........
options: the centre line of the approach area coincides with that of the runway
approach areas are measured in horizontal surfaces
the imaginary inclined plane which is directly above the approach area is called approach surface
explain: These are the standard geometric definitions for the 'approach zone' used to ensure obstacle-free flight paths.

q: 14. Pick up the correct abbreviation from the following ...........
explain: These are all standard abbreviations used in aviation navigation and communications.

q: 15. In instrument landing system ...........
options: L.O.M. and L.M.M. are installed on one side and localizer antenna on the other side
L.O.M. and localizer are installed on one side and L.M.M. on the other side
localizer and L.M.M. are installed on one side and L.O.M. on the other side
explain: The Localizer is at the far end of the runway, while Marker Beacons (Outer/Middle) are located along the approach path.

q: 16. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following ...........
options: L.O.M. is installed at 7.2 km from the threshold
L.M.M. is installed at 1.0 km from the threshold
localizer antenna is installed at 300 m from the other end of the runway
Glide slope antenna is installed at the centre of the runway about 150 m on one side
explain: The Glide Slope antenna is not in the 'centre' of the runway; it is offset to the side (usually 120-150m from centerline) to avoid being a collision hazard.

q: 17. Pick up the correct statement from the following ...........
options: runway edge from the landing side, is called threshold
localizer indicates to the pilot his position with respect to the proposed alignment
the glide slope indicates the correct angle of descent
explain: These descriptions accurately define the landing threshold and the components of the ILS (horizontal and vertical guidance).

q: 18. Pick up the correct statement from the following ...........
options: approximate geometric centre of the landing area, is called air port reference point
the boundaries of horizontal surface and conical surface are marked with reference to air port reference point
the location of the air port on a map is the position of air port reference point
explain: The Airport Reference Point (ARP) is the designated geographical center used for navigation and defining obstacle limitation surfaces.

q: 19. Pick up the correct statement from the following ...........
options: approach zone survey is carried out to determine the elevations of the protruding obstructions above horizontal, conical and transitional surface
the wind data of an air port is depicted in the form of a chart known as wind rose
the landing and takeoff of the air craft is made against the wind direction
explain: These are three fundamental pillars of airport site selection and runway orientation.

q: 20. For the proposed air port, the survey project provides ...........
explain: Airport planning requires a comprehensive set of documents covering long-term development (Master Plan), terrain (Topographic), and earthwork (Grading).

q: 21. According to I.C.A.O. the recommended length of air ports is decided on ...........
explain: Basic runway length must be corrected for elevation, temperature, and gradient to reach the final design length.

q: 22. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following
options: L.O.M. is located at a distance of 7.2 km from runway end
L.M.M. is located at a distance of 1 km from runway end
localizer is located at a distance of 300 m from the centre of the runway
explain: The distances provided for ILS components (Outer Marker, Middle Marker, and Localizer) are within standard operational ranges.

q: 23. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: the beginning of the runway is known as threshold
localizer indicates the position of the aircraft with respect to the alignment of the runway
the glide slope antenna indicates the position of the aircraft with respect to the glide path
threshold markings are provided at each end of the runway
explain: All points correctly describe the functional components of runway navigation and marking systems.

q: 24. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: geometric centre of the airport is known as airport reference point (ARP)
the boundaries of an airport are marked with reference to A.R.P.
the position of airport is located by A.R.P. relative to the nearest city
explain: The ARP serves as the official designated center point of an airport for all geographical and administrative purposes.

q: 25. Pick up the correct statement from the following ...........
options: the basic length of a runway is increased at a rate of 7% per 300 m of elevation of M.S.L.
the standard temperature at the site is obtained by reducing the standard sea level temperature of 15°C at the rate of 6.5°C per 1000 m rise in elevation
the acrodrome reference temperature is the monthly mean of the mean daily temperature for the hottest month of the year
explain: These are the three standard ICAO rules for calculating runway length corrections based on site conditions.

q: 26. Pick up the correct statement from the following ...........
options: the distance between the points of intersection of the extreme tangents to the transition curve is kept greater than 7500 m × sum of grade changes at the point of intersection
the rate of change of grade is limited to 0.3% per 30 m length of the curve
according to I.C.A.O. the maximum longitudinal gradient along a runway is limited to 1.5%
explain: These parameters govern the vertical alignment and longitudinal profile of the runway to ensure smooth transitions for fast-moving aircraft.

q: 27. A gradient of + 0.08% is following by a gradient of - 0.07%. If the permissible rate of change of grade is 0.003 per 30 metres, the length of the transition curve, is ...........
explain: The total change in grade is $0.08 - (-0.07) = 0.15%$. At a rate of $0.003$ per $30m$, the required length is $(0.15 / 0.03) \times 30 = 150m$.

q: 28. For the taxiways, the following statement is true ...........
options: the permissible rate of grade is 1%
explain: Taxiways have more flexible gradient requirements than runways, allowing for steeper longitudinal and transverse slopes as aircraft move at lower speeds.

q: 29. Two single runways may be arranged so as to have ...........
explain: Runway configurations are chosen based on wind coverage; L, T, and X shapes (intersecting or open-V) are common to handle varying wind directions.

q: 30. The threshold markings are ...........
explain: Threshold markings consist of a pattern of longitudinal stripes of uniform dimensions (typically $45m$ long, $4m$ wide with $1m$ spacing) symmetrically placed about the centerline.

q: 31. Total correction for elevation and temperature should not be more than
explain: ICAO guidelines state that the combined correction for altitude and temperature should not exceed 35% of basic length.

q: 32. As per I.C.A.O., for A, B, and C type of airports, maximum effective, transverse and longitudinal grades in percentage respectively are ...........
explain: These are the strict gradient limits for high-class airports to ensure safety during high-speed operations.

q: 33. As per I.C.A.O. recommendation, the rate of change of longitudinal gradient per 30 m length of vertical curve for A and B type of airports is limited to a maximum of ...........
explain: To ensure pilot comfort and aircraft structural integrity, the rate of change for major airports (A and B) is restricted to $0.1%$ per $30m$.

q: 34. According to I.C.A.O. all markings on runways are painted
explain: Runway markings are mandatory white to ensure high contrast against the asphalt or concrete surface.

q: 35. The threshold markings are
options: placed symmetrically on either side of the runway centre line
explain: Threshold markings consist of a pattern of longitudinal stripes of uniform dimensions disposed symmetrically about the centerline of a runway.

q: 36. *For night landing, the thresholds are lighted
explain: Threshold lights are fixed unidirectional lights showing green in the direction of approach to the runway.

q: 37. Zero fuel weight of an aircraft is ............
options: equal to sum of empty operating weight and the maximum pay load
explain: Zero Fuel Weight (ZFW) is the total weight of the aircraft and all its contents (including passengers and cargo), but excluding the total weight of the usable fuel on board.

q: 38. As per I.C.A.O., for airports serving big aircrafts, the crosswind component should not exceed ............
explain: For large aircraft, the crosswind component is restricted to 35 kmph (approx 19 knots) for safe landing and takeoff operations.

q: 39. Calm period is the percentage of time during which wind intensity is less than ............
explain: The 'Calm Period' refers to the time when wind velocity remains below 6.4 kmph (4 mph).

q: 40. According to I.C.A.O., all markings on the runways are ............
explain: Runway markings are consistently white to provide contrast against the dark pavement. Taxiway markings are yellow.

q: 41. The width and interval of transverse centre line bars along the extended centre line bars along the extended centre line of runway, in approach lighting system are ............
explain: Standard approach lighting systems (like Calvert) use transverse bars of specific widths (4.2m) at 30m intervals.

q: 42. In instrumental landing system, the middle markers are located ............
options: along the extended centre line of runway end
about 1 km ahead of the runway threshold
about 7 km ahead of the runway threshold
explain: The middle marker (MM) is usually positioned about 1 km from the threshold to inform the pilot they are close to the decision height.

q: 43. The size of landing area for multiengine helicopters operating under I.F.R. conditions is ............
explain: Under Instrument Flight Rules (IFR), larger landing areas are required for safety; 60m x 120m is a standard for multiengine operations.

q: 44. The centre to centre spacing of heliport lighting along the periphery of landing and takeoff area should be ............
explain: Lighting on the periphery of a heliport is typically spaced at 7.5 meters to define the touchdown and lift-off area clearly.

q: 45. The slope of the obstruction clearance line from the boundary of the heliport should be ............
explain: Heliports require an obstruction-free path, typically defined by a 1:8 slope starting from the heliport boundary.

q: 46. If d is the deceleration in m/sec² and V is the speed in kmph, then the stopping distance of an aircraft is given by ............
explain: Converted from $v^2 = 2as$. Since $V$ is in kmph, conversion factors result in $V^2 / 25.5d$.

q: 47. As per UK design criteria, if L.C.N. of aircraft is between 1.25 to 1.5 times the L.C.N. of pavement, then the number of movements allowed are ............
explain: The Load Classification Number (LCN) system restricts movements if the aircraft exceeds pavement capacity; 300 movements is a common safety threshold.

q: 48. The main disadvantage of angle nose out parking configuration of aircraft is that the ............
options: aircraft rear loading door is far away from terminal building
hot blast is directed towards the terminal building
overall apron area required is more
explain: Angle nose out parking causes the engine exhaust (hot blast) to point directly at the terminal, creating safety and comfort issues.

q: 49. A flexible pavement of runway consists of
options: finishing coarse, surface course and base course
surface course, base course and sub-base course
base course, sub-base course and rough course
explain: Flexible pavements consist of the surface course, base course, and sub-base course over the subgrade.

q: 50. Which of the following is used for servicing and repairs of the aircraft?
explain: A hangar is a closed building structure used to hold aircraft in protective storage or for maintenance and repair.
